findings.summary: docs/system-facts.md is not among the reading's deliverables
findings.evidence: A change outside the listed deliverables widens the scope.

findings.summary: The ~100-token planner.md rule breaks the existing under-500-token cap on planner.md, so cargo test fails.
findings.evidence:
lib.rs:402 asserts `estimate_tokens(frame.text) < 500` for PLANNER_FRAME. estimate_tokens is ceil(bytes/3) (lib.rs:73-75). compose joins trimmed parts with "

" plus "
" (lib.rs:142-148). With system facts 'budget planner: 806' and 'budget contract: 326', planner.md is about 2418 - 978 - 3 ≈ 1437 bytes ≈ 480 tokens (computed, not run). The plan adds about 300 bytes, giving about 580 tokens, so the test fails. The plan's budget reasoning (and the reading's '494 tokens of headroom') counts only against the 1300 set budget. Fix: Make planner.md room by condensing existing bullets, or keep the new planner.md text to about 50 bytes (for example one clause appended to the demonstrations bullet), and put the full wording in the planner_brief Report section, which is outside the budget sets. Name `planner_and_critic_frames_are_short_and_fit_the_budgets` in the criterion 2 and 7 demonstrations. Add a step that checks planner.md stays under 500 tokens.
findings.location: Plan step 5 / decision 6 / risk 'The planner prompt grows past its budget'; crates/athena-context/src/lib.rs:394-404

findings.summary: The new planner rule tells the planner to run a command it cannot run, so the planning-stage gate would be satisfied by invented results.
findings.evidence: planning_grant gives the planner and critic tools [Read, Grep, Glob], no commands and no writes ('No Bash, no git command'). planner.md line 3 says 'Read, Grep and Glob only'. A rule to run cargo test and cite its results cannot be followed. The planner would then claim results it never measured, which is the reasoning-instead-of-executing fault this job is meant to remove. Fix: Reword the rule for what the planner can do: read crates/athena-core/tests/refusal_corpus.rs; map every input form the rule handles to an existing corpus case by id, or list the case a producer step adds; and make `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus` the demonstration the producer and verifier run. Pin those words in the briefs test.
findings.location: Plan step 5 and Files entry for planner.md (rule text 'runs `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus` ... cites the results'); crates/athena-core/src/run/planning.rs:565-574

findings.summary: The plan does not mention the existing replay of real past accepted readings or explain how the corpus relates to it.
findings.evidence: replay_cases already runs the newest accepted readings from records through the base and candidate checkers at verification, and holds a candidate that newly refuses more than its declared share. That covers 'real past requests' on the accept side only, and only after code is written. Fix: Add a decision explaining that the corpus is the planning-time, refuse-side complement to the verify-time replay: replay uses records/ that the planner cannot see, and holds only accepted readings. The CHANGELOG and decisions entries should say the same.

findings.summary: The coverage test covers only check_* steps in refusing_check, not the parser, stems or stop lists named in the root cause.
findings.evidence: The extractor matches `step!\((check_[a-z_]+)\(`. A new matching helper inside an existing check, or a change to is_bullet or request_text_acceptance, needs no new corpus case. The 2bpc gaps were exactly parser and stem/stop-list order. The pinned bullet counts cover today's parser only. Fix: State this limit in the decisions entry and the test header, and name it as residual risk the planner rule covers. Optionally also require that every case's bullet count is asserted, so a parser change must touch the corpus.

findings.summary: Other callers of check_reading_acceptance (the reader loop, check_reading_text, replay) should be noted as unaffected.
findings.evidence: check_reading_acceptance is called at reading.rs:637 and by check_reading_text at 3427, which feeds BinaryChecker replay. Their refusal text must not change. Fix: In the risks, name these callers and note that the existing replay and check-reading tests already guard the error text.

summary: The plan matches the accepted reading: a Rust fixture corpus in crates/athena-core/tests/refusal_corpus.rs run through the real gate; a `refusing_check` refactor that keeps the check order (confirmed at reading.rs:3020-3025) and names the refusing check with stringify!; a test that reads reading.rs and fails when a check has no refusing case; and a planner rule. The seams exist today: the six checks, `continued_jobs`, `request_text_acceptance`, `planner_brief`, `planner_inputs`, PLANNER_FRAME and the regex dependency. `is_bullet` does skip `1)` and `(a)`, so the pinned 0-bullet results are right. Two problems need a revision. First, the plan adds about 300 bytes to planner.md, but `planner_and_critic_frames_are_short_and_fit_the_budgets` (athena-context/src/lib.rs:402) requires planner.md alone to be under 500 tokens. Computed from the system-facts lines (planner set 806, contract 326), planner.md is about 480 tokens now, so it has about 55 bytes of room. As written, cargo test fails (criterion 7). Second, the rule tells the planner to run `cargo test` and cite the results, but planners and critics get only Read, Grep and Glob (planning_grant, run/planning.rs:565-574). The planner cannot do this, and the rule invites invented results, which is the failure class this job targets. Minor points: the plan ignores the existing verify-time replay of real past readings (replay_cases, reading.rs:3514); the coverage test covers only check_* steps and not parser, stem or stop-list helpers; and `refusing_check` should note that check_reading_text and the reader loop (reading.rs:637, 3427) still go through the wrapper. Athena's own finding on docs/system-facts.md is outweighed: the budgets test needs that edit.
